name: HalluQA
intro: HalluQA 是针对中文大模型幻觉的 450 题问答基准，由 175 道误导题、69 道高难误导题和 206 道知识题组成，共覆盖 30 个领域。数据以 GLM-130B、ChatGPT 与 Puyu 的稳定错误作为对抗性筛选信号，并由作者或 NLP 专家复核问题、答案和外部依据。
build_method: 人工编题、模型对抗筛选、专家质检
task_type: 开放式问答, 幻觉评判
eval_feature: 对抗性、中文原生、GPT-4 五票判定
scale: 450（175 误导题 + 69 高难误导题 + 206 知识题；30 个领域）
build_method_en: Human authoring, model-based adversarial selection, expert quality control
intro_en: HalluQA is a 450-question benchmark for hallucinations in Chinese LLMs, comprising 175 misleading questions, 69 misleading-hard questions, and 206 knowledge questions across 30 domains. Stable failures from GLM-130B, ChatGPT, and Puyu serve as adversarial selection signals, while authors or an NLP expert verify questions, answer sets, and external evidence.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with HalluQA arXiv:2310.03368v4, official repository commit c025c0d, and HalluQA.json SHA-256 prefix e2f8ac3. The pinned JSON has 450 rows: 175 misleading, 69 misleading-hard, and 206 knowledge questions across 30 domains. The misleading branch adapts 20 TruthfulQA-style patterns to Chinese contexts, uses six manual QA demonstrations, probes GLM-130B five times, and retains questions with imitative falsehoods in at least 3/5 runs. The misleading-hard branch starts from recent Chinese Internet confusions and uses ChatGPT 3.5 to create adversarial questions; it is not described as a set of ChatGPT failures. Ten Chinese-native graduate interns write knowledge candidates; ChatGPT and Puyu each answer five times, both must fail at least 3/5, and an NLP expert reduces about 1,000 candidates to 206. Misleading items receive four correct and four wrong answers; knowledge items receive at least one of each. External links validate knowledge items, while authors independent of misleading-question authoring rewrite or discard defects. GPT-4-0613 judges every response using correct-answer examples, five votes, temperature 0, and top-p 0.5. The paper text lists five criteria; the pinned script calculate_metrics.py expresses the same semantics as six numbered prompt bullets by separating semantic equivalence. The consistency study uses 100 questions, six models, and 600 outputs, reporting 93.5% agreement for five-vote judgments. The metric is non-hallucination rate; refusal is a hallucination unless the reference says the question is unanswerable.
